intended_object: The canonical intertwiner S = Q P + (1−Q)(1−P) of two closed subspaces U, V (P, Q their orthogonal projections), viewed as an invertible element of the group of units of B(H). It is invertible when U and V are uniformly acute (‖1 − S‖ < 1). This comes from the docstring and from how the Davis–Kahan / direct-rotation (Kato) development uses it.
explanation:
The body is `Units.oneSub (1 − S) h`, where `h` is the proof that ‖1 − S‖ < 1. `Units.oneSub t` is the Neumann-series unit whose underlying element is 1 − t. So the underlying operator is 1 − (1 − S) = S, which is exactly the canonical intertwiner. The library proves this as `coe_spectraCanonicalIntertwinerUnit`.

`spectraCanonicalIntertwiner` is defined as `V.starProjection * U.starProjection + Vᗮ.starProjection * Uᗮ.starProjection`. That is the standard Kato/Davis–Kahan operator QP + (1−Q)(1−P).

The setting is natural: any complete inner product space over ℝ or ℂ (via `RCLike`), where the Neumann series needs completeness. Mathlib has no general version of this specific construction. The definition is essentially a bundling of an existing operator with its invertibility proof, and it does this correctly.
